rules.title: Statewide rent cap (AB 1482 / Civil Code § 1947.12)
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot increase rent more than 5% plus the local CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, over any 12-month period.

coverage_conditions.text: Residential real property means any dwelling or unit that is intended for human habitation, including any dwelling or unit in a mobilehome park.

rules.exemptions: Exemptions include: housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); deed-restricted affordable housing; dormitories; single-family homes and condos owned by non-corporate entities who provide required notice; duplexes where owner occupies one unit; and housing subject to local rent control that is more restrictive.
rules.interaction: Yields to the listed local rules where they cover the building (state rule becomes superseded).
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase

rules.title: California Statewide Just Cause Eviction Requirement
rules.requirement: After 12 months of continuous lawful occupancy, landlords must have just cause (either at-fault or no-fault) to terminate a tenancy and must state the cause in writing.

coverage_conditions.text: Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome, is exempt. Single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms are exempt. A property containing two separate dwelling units within a single structure in which the owner occupied one of the units as the owner's principal place of residence at the beginning of the tenancy is exempt (up to 2 units). Alienable residential real property (condos) owned by individuals (not REITs, corporations, or LLCs with corporate members) are exempt if proper notice is provided.

rules.exemptions: Exemptions include: transient/tourist hotels, certain institutional housing, dormitories, shared bathroom/kitchen with owner, single-family owner-occupied residences (≤2 units), duplex with owner-occupied unit, housing <15 years old (except mobilehomes), alienable single units owned by natural persons (with notice), deed-restricted affordable housing, mobilehome owners (not renters).
rules.interaction: Yields to the listed local rules where they cover the building (state rule becomes superseded).
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy

rules.title: California No-Fault Just Cause Eviction Relocation Assistance
rules.requirement: When a landlord terminates a tenancy for a no-fault just cause reason, the landlord must provide relocation assistance equal to one month's rent or waive the final month's rent.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to residential real property subject to just cause eviction requirements under this section (same exemptions as the just cause requirement apply).

rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the just cause eviction requirement. Relocation assistance is credited against any other relocation assistance required by any other law.
rules.quoted_span:
For a tenancy for which just cause is required to terminate the tenancy under subdivision (a), if an owner of residential real property issues a termination notice based on a no-fault just cause described in paragraph (2) of subdivision (b), the owner shall, regardless of the tenant’s income, at the owner’s option, do one of the following:
(A) Assist the tenant to relocate by providing a direct payment to the tenant as described in paragraph (3).
(B) Waive in writing the payment of rent for the final month of the tenancy, prior to the rent becoming due

rules.title: Photograph unit before or at start of new tenancy
rules.requirement: Landlords must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy that begins on or after July 1, 2025 to document its condition.

coverage_conditions.text: tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025

rules.quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit

rules.title: Security deposit return deadline
rules.requirement: Landlords must return the security deposit or any remaining portion within 21 days after the tenant leaves the unit.
rules.quoted_span:
All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned
within 21 days
after the tenant/s leave the unit vacant

rules.title: Itemized statement and proof of repairs required
rules.requirement: If a landlord deducts from the security deposit, they must provide an itemized statement and copies of bills, invoices, or receipts showing the charges for repairs or cleaning.
rules.quoted_span: If deductions were made, the landlord must give the tenant a written statement itemizing the amount of and and purpose for any security deposit deductions, accompanied by copies of documents showing charges incurred and deducted by the landlord to repair or clean the premises, including a copy of any bill, invoice, or receipt for materials or supplies deductions

rules.title: Proof of completed repairs required
rules.requirement: Beginning January 1, 2025, landlords must provide proof that necessary repairs for which they deducted from the security deposit were completed.
rules.quoted_span: Starting January 1, 2025, landlords must provide proof that necessary repairs were completed

rules.title: Photographs after regaining possession required
rules.requirement: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must photograph a unit after regaining possession but before making any repairs or cleaning for which they intend to deduct from the security deposit.
rules.quoted_span: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit

rules.title: Maximum security deposit – one month's rent (general rule)
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot demand or receive a security deposit exceeding one month's rent, plus first month's rent, except under specified exceptions.

coverage_conditions.text: rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant

rules.exemptions: Small landlords (natural persons owning ≤2 properties with ≤4 total units) may charge up to 2 months' rent except for service members. Service members cannot be charged more than 1 month's rent.
rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy

rules.title: Application screening fee cap and consumer protections
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge more than $30 per applicant for an application screening fee, with annual CPI adjustments allowed since 1998.

coverage_conditions.text: residential rental property

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to federal or state housing assistance programs with their own deposit and fee regulations.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998

rules.title: Source of Income Protection
rules.requirement: California law prohibits housing providers from discriminating against tenants based on their source of income, including government rental assistance such as Section 8 vouchers and disability benefits.

coverage_conditions.text: Most housing accommodations in California, including single-family homes, multi-family homes, condominiums, apartments, short-term rentals, mobile homes, subsidized housing, dormitories, sober living facilities, group homes, residential motels, emergency shelters, homeless shelters, shelters for survivors of domestic violence, recreational vehicles (RVs) used as a home, farmworker housing, and boats used as homes.

rules.exemptions: When an owner is occupying a home and is renting to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”). This includes the State of California’s COVID-19 Rent Relief Program, Housing Choice (Section 8) vouchers, (SSI) social security disability benefits, or wages earned from a job

rules.title: Criminal History Screening Restrictions
rules.requirement: California law prohibits housing providers from considering arrests without convictions, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and bans blanket policies that refuse to rent to anyone with a criminal history.

coverage_conditions.text: Most housing accommodations in California, including single-family homes, multi-family homes, condominiums, apartments, short-term rentals, mobile homes, subsidized housing, dormitories, sober living facilities, group homes, residential motels, emergency shelters, homeless shelters, shelters for survivors of domestic violence, recreational vehicles (RVs) used as a home, farmworker housing, and boats used as homes.

rules.exemptions: When an owner is occupying a home and is renting to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history

rules.title: Prohibition on source-of-income discrimination in housing
rules.requirement: It is unlawful for a housing owner to discriminate against or harass any person because of their source of income.

coverage_conditions.text: All housing accommodations in California

rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful:
(a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person

rules.title: Prohibition on source-of-income inquiries in advertising
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to publish any advertisement for housing that indicates a preference, limitation, or discrimination based on source of income.

coverage_conditions.text: All housing accommodations in California

rules.quoted_span: For any person to make, print, or publish, or cause to be made, printed, or published any notice, statement, or advertisement, with respect to the sale or rental of a housing accommodation that indicates any preference, limitation, or discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information or an intention to make that preference, limitation, or discrimination

rules.title: Income standards must be based on tenant-paid portion of rent for subsidized tenants
rules.requirement: For tenants with government rent subsidies, landlords must base income standards on the portion of rent the tenant will pay, not the total rent.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies when there is a government rent subsidy

rules.quoted_span:
In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:
(A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant

rules.title: Alternative evidence for credit history for subsidized tenants
rules.requirement: When using credit history to screen subsidized tenants, landlords must offer applicants the option to provide alternative evidence of ability to pay, such as government benefit payments, pay records, or bank statements.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies when there is a government rent subsidy and landlord uses credit history in screening

rules.quoted_span:
Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements

rules.title: Definition of source of income includes government housing subsidies
rules.requirement: Source of income includes lawful, verifiable income such as public assistance and housing subsidies, including Section 8 vouchers, paid to or on behalf of a tenant.

coverage_conditions.text: All housing accommodations in California

rules.quoted_span: For the purposes of this section, “source of income” means lawful, verifiable income paid directly to a tenant, or to a representative of a tenant, or paid to a housing owner or landlord on behalf of a tenant, including federal, state, or local public assistance, and federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including, but not limited to, federal housing assistance vouchers issued under Section 8 of the United States Housing Act of 1937 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 1437f)

rules.title: Prohibition on using or distributing common pricing algorithms as part of restraint of trade
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce.
rules.exemptions: Does not include the end consumer of a product or service
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter

rules.title: Prohibition on coercing adoption of algorithm-recommended prices
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt the algorithm's recommended price or commercial term.
rules.exemptions: Does not include the end consumer of a product or service
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm if the person coerces another person to set or adopt a recommended price or commercial term recommended by the common pricing algorithm for the same or similar products or services in the jurisdiction of this state

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act Good Cause Requirement for Eviction or Non-Renewal
rules.requirement: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant and must describe the cause in detail in a written notice, except for nonpayment of rent.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord must have 
good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53). There are several grounds for a good cause 
eviction. Each cause, except for nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail by the landlord 
in a written notice to the tenant

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act Good Cause Requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords in New Jersey can only evict tenants for good cause as enumerated in the Anti-Eviction Act, which applies to most residential rental properties.

coverage_conditions.text: This law may not apply to two - or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units. It does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant.

rules.exemptions: May not apply to owner-occupied two- or three-unit properties with two or fewer rental units; does not apply to transient hotel/motel guests or seasonal tenants in guest houses.
rules.quoted_span:
The Anti-Eviction Act applies to most residential rental properties including single-family 
homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes

rules.title: Stay of Eviction for Special Circumstances
rules.requirement: A tenant may request a court-ordered stay of eviction due to special circumstances for up to one year unless the landlord and tenant agree to an extension.
rules.quoted_span:
A tenant may ask the court for permission to stay in the premises due to special 
circumstances that moving may cause. This action is a stay of eviction. If permission is granted, 
the tenant may not stay in the premises for more than one year, unless there is an agreed upon 
extension between landlord and tenant

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act Good Cause Requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord may only recover possession of a residential dwelling unit by tenant consent or through the legal eviction process.

coverage_conditions.text: dwelling unit used as a residence

rules.quoted_span:
A landlord may recover possession of a dwelling unit used as a residence only by 
consent of the tenants or through the legal process of eviction. In  an eviction action, when a 
landlord obtains a judgment of possession of the unit from a court, the landlord is entitled to a 
warrant for removal

rules.title: Notice requirements for rent increase eviction under Anti-Eviction Act
rules.requirement: Before evicting a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, a landlord must serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase, and the increase must not be unconscionable.
rules.quoted_span:
This law provides that before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of 
an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent 
increase

rules.title: Eviction for Disorderly Conduct - Notice Requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict for disorderly conduct after giving a written Notice to Cease and serving a Notice to Quit at least three days before filing suit.
rules.quoted_span:
If after given written Notice to Cease disorderly conduct, the tenant continues the 
disorderly conduct and that conduct destroys the peace and quiet of the other tenants living 
in the building or neighborhood, the landlord may file a suite for eviction. A Notice to Quit 
must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction

rules.title: Eviction for Damage to Property - Notice Requirement
rules.requirement: Tenants who intentionally or through gross negligence damage property may be evicted after receiving a Notice to Quit at least three days before suit is filed.
rules.quoted_span:
The tenant may be evicted if they have intentionally or by reason of gross negligence 
caused or allowed destruction, damage, or injury to the property. A Notice to Quit must be 
served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction

rules.title: Eviction for Violation of Rules - Notice Requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict for continued substantial breach of reasonable rules after giving a Notice to Cease and a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing suit, with notices given on or before the start of a new month.
rules.quoted_span:
If after given a written Notice to Cease violating or breaching reasonable rules and 
regulations contained in the lease or accepted in writing by the tenant, the tenant continues 
to substantially violate or breach the rules and regulations, the  landlord may file a suit for 
eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing 
the suit for eviction

rules.title: Eviction for Failure to Pay Rent Increase
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted for refusing to pay a rent increase that is not unconscionable and complies with rent control laws, after receiving a Notice to Quit at least one month before suit is filed.
rules.quoted_span:
If a tenant fails to pay rent after being given notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, 
the landlord may file a suit for eviction

rules.title: Eviction for Permanent Retirement from Residential Use - Notice Requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict to permanently retire property from residential use after serving a Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing suit, and no action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.quoted_span:
If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential 
use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord 
may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months 
prior to filing the suit for eviction

rules.title: Eviction for Refusal to Accept Lease Changes - Notice Requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict when a lease expires if the tenant refuses reasonable changes to lease terms, after giving written notice and serving a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing suit.
rules.quoted_span:
When the lease expires, the landlord may propose reasonable but substantial changes to the 
terms and conditions of the lease

rules.title: Eviction for Habitual Late Rent Payment - Notice Requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict for habitual late rent payment after giving a Notice to Cease and serving a Notice to Quit at least one month before filing suit.
rules.quoted_span:
If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to 
Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the 
tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction

rules.title: Eviction After Conversion - Owner Occupancy (Post-Recording Tenancy)
rules.requirement: An owner may evict a tenant whose tenancy began after the condominium or cooperative conversion was recorded if the owner has contracted to sell the unit to a buyer who will personally occupy it, after serving a Notice to Quit at least two months before filing suit.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of a building or mobile home park, which 
is constructed as or being converted to a condominium, cooperative or fee simple 
ownership, seeks to evict a tenant or sublessee whose initial tenancy began after the master 
deed, or agreement establishing the cooperative or subdivision plat was recorded, because 
the owner has contracted to sell the unit to a buyer who seeks to personally occupy it and 
the contract for sale calls for the unit to be vacant at the time of closing

rules.title: Eviction for Employment Termination
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant whose residence is conditioned on employment by the landlord, after serving a Notice to Quit three days before filing suit.
rules.quoted_span:
If a tenant resides in the property on the condition that, he is employed by the landlord as 
a superintendent, janitor, or in some other job and that employment is terminated the 
landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three 
days prior to filing a suit for eviction

rules.title: Penalty for False Owner-Occupancy Eviction
rules.requirement: If a tenant vacates after receiving notice of landlord's personal occupancy and the landlord fails to occupy the unit for at least six months, the landlord is liable for three times damages plus attorney fees.
rules.quoted_span:
When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the  landlord 
wishes to personally occupy the unit the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six (6) months. 
If instead the landlord permits personal occupancy of the unit by another tenant or registration of 
conversion of the property to a condominium or cooperative, the landlord is liable to the former 
tenant for three (3) times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs

rules.title: Penalty for False Permanent Retirement Eviction
rules.requirement: If a tenant vacates after notice of permanent retirement from residential use and the landlord uses the property residentially within five years, the landlord is liable for three times damages plus attorney fees and a civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation.
rules.quoted_span:
When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord seeks 
to permanently board up or demolish the building or to permanently retire it from residential use, 
the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years. If the 
landlord allows any residential use of the unit during the five (5) year period from the date the unit 
became vacant, the landlord, or the former landlord, may be liable to the tenant for three (3) times 
the damages plus attorney fees and costs. Additionally, the landlord or former landlord may be 
liable for a civil penalty up to $10,000.00 for each violation of this law

rules.title: Self-Help Eviction Prohibition
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot evict tenants by force or lockout without a court order and may be liable for damages if they attempt a self-help eviction.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord or any other person who enters an apartment or property without a court 
order authorizing such entry and/or holds a tenant’s belongings unlawfully by force or threat of 
monies owed may be liable for damages to the tenant

rules.title: Prohibition on Retaliatory Eviction
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from retaliatory eviction or lease alteration when tenants exercise civil rights such as enforcing lease rights, making good faith complaints to authorities about health or safety violations, or joining tenant organizations.

coverage_conditions.text: all rental properties used for dwelling purposes, including mobile homes, except owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord cannot take reprisal action against a tenant by eviction, substantial alteration of 
a lease or its terms, or refusal to renew a lease when a tenant exercises certain civil rights

rules.title: Post-Foreclosure Tenant Notification Requirement
rules.requirement: The new owner of a foreclosed property must notify tenants in English and Spanish within 10 business days after the sale that ownership has changed and that they are not required to move due to the foreclosure.
rules.quoted_span:
Any person acquiring a foreclosed property containing one or more residential rental units 
must provide notices to the tenants in English and Spanish, within 10 business days after the sale, 
letting tenants know that ownership has changed hands and that the tenants are not required to 
move because of the foreclosure

rules.title: Landlord Registration Requirement - Eviction Prohibition
rules.requirement: A landlord is prohibited from evicting a tenant if the landlord has not been properly registered.

coverage_conditions.text: one or two-family non-owner-occupied home and buildings with three or more units

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two-family homes are exempt from registration requirement
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord 
registration law prohibits a landlord from evicting a tenant in the building if the landlord has not 
been properly registered (N.J.S.A. 46:8-27 to -37)

rules.title: Return of security deposit after tenancy termination
rules.requirement: A landlord must return the tenant's security deposit plus interest, minus any lawful deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless tenant sends written request to apply the law after 30 days.
rules.quoted_span:
Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security 
deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant

rules.title: Return of security deposit after displacement by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation
rules.requirement: When a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation and an official prohibits occupancy or certifies displacement longer than seven days, the landlord must return the security deposit within five business days.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless tenant sends written request to apply the law after 30 days.
rules.quoted_span:
Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or 
evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit

rules.title: Maximum security deposit limit
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot collect a security deposit that exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless tenant sends written request to apply the law after 30 days.
rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent

rules.title: Security Deposit Return for Service Members
rules.requirement: When a service member terminates their lease under the Service Members Civil Relief Act, the landlord must return the security deposit in accordance with New Jersey's security deposit law.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies when service member properly terminates lease under Service Members Civil Relief Act.

rules.quoted_span:
The landlord is required to return the security 
deposit in accordance with the applicable Security Deposit Law (N.J.S.A. 46:8-26)

rules.title: Security Deposit Return for Domestic Violence Lease Termination
rules.requirement: When a tenant terminates their lease due to domestic violence under the Safe Housing Act, the landlord must return the security deposit plus interest within 15 business days after the lease terminates.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to tenants terminating lease under Safe Housing Act; does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.
rules.quoted_span:
Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available 
the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s 
agent

rules.title: Residential rental property application fee cap
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot charge more than $50 for an application fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property (adjusted annually for inflation).

coverage_conditions.text: Exempts dwelling units in one- or two-family dwellings offered for rent, and real estate licensees unless they are the landlord.

rules.exemptions: Does not apply to dwelling units in one- or two-family dwellings offered for rent, or to real estate licensees (unless licensee is the landlord).
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50

rules.title: Prohibition on source-of-income discrimination in housing
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot discriminate against tenants or purchasers based on their source of lawful income, including Section 8 vouchers.
rules.exemptions: Exemptions include: rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where owner occupies the other unit; rental of rooms in a one-family dwelling occupied by the owner; and religious organization preferences.
rules.quoted_span:
The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based
on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent
or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses. This
means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
income

rules.title: Source of income discrimination prohibition
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from discriminating against tenants based on their source of lawful income when renting housing.

coverage_conditions.text: The law applies to all landlord-tenant relationships, except those involving two-family owner occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex, i.e. YMCA and age-restricted housing, as it pertains to familial status.

rules.exemptions: Exempt for two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in owner or resident-occupied single homes, and single-sex residences like YMCA and age-restricted housing (familial status only).
rules.quoted_span:
The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, 
ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act – Ban-the-Box and Criminal Record Screening Restrictions
rules.requirement: Housing providers cannot ask about or consider an applicant's criminal record until after making a conditional offer, with narrow exceptions for methamphetamine manufacture in federally assisted housing and lifetime sex offender registration.

coverage_conditions.text: Applies to rental dwelling units except dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are exempt.
rules.quoted_span:
A
housing provider
shall not require an applicant to
complete any housing application that includes any inquiries regarding an
applicant’s criminal record prior to the provision of a conditional offer,
except that a housing provider may consider whether an applicant has ever been
convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production
of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether
the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State
sex offender registration program

rules.title: Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act - prohibition on use of algorithmic pricing coordinators
rules.requirement: Rental property owners are prohibited from using coordinator services that employ algorithmic devices to set or recommend rents using competitively sensitive information from multiple landlords, and coordinators are prohibited from performing such coordinating functions.

coverage_conditions.text: applies to rental property owners of residential dwelling units in New Jersey

rules.title: Fourteen-day notice to quit for nonpayment of rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may terminate a written lease for nonpayment of rent by giving fourteen days' written notice to quit, unless the tenant pays all rent due with interest and costs by the answer date.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit

rules.title: Notice requirements to terminate estate at will tenancies
rules.requirement: A landlord must give a tenant at will three months' written notice to terminate the tenancy, or if rent is paid more frequently than every three months, notice equal to the rent payment interval or thirty days, whichever is longer.

coverage_conditions.text: Estates at will

rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent with cure right
rules.requirement: For nonpayment of rent, a landlord must give fourteen days' written notice to quit, but a tenant who has not received a similar notice in the past twelve months can prevent termination by paying the full rent due within ten days.

coverage_conditions.text: Tenant at will

rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due

rules.title: Anti-retaliation protection for tenant complaints and organizing
rules.requirement: Landlords who retaliate against tenants for reporting code violations, pursuing legal action to enforce housing laws, or organizing tenant unions are liable for damages of at least one month's rent up to three months' rent or actual damages (whichever is greater), plus costs and attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: 1-3 months' rent or actual damages (whichever is greater)

coverage_conditions.text: residential premises

rules.quoted_span: Any person or agent thereof who threatens to or takes reprisals against any tenant of residential premises for the tenant's act of, commencing, proceeding with, or obtaining relief in any judicial or administrative action the purpose of which action is to obtain damages under, or otherwise enforce, any federal, state or local law, regulation, by-law or ordinance, which has as its objective the regulation of residential premises; or exercising the tenant's rights pursuant to section one hundred and twenty-four D of chapter one hundred and sixty-four; or reporting to the board of health or, in the city of Boston to the commissioner of housing inspection or to any other board having as its objective the regulation of residential premises a violation or a suspected violation of any health or building code or of any other municipal by-law or ordinance, or state or federal law or regulation which has as its objective the regulation of residential premises; or reporting or complaining of such violation or suspected violation in writing to the landlord or to the agent of the landlord; or for organizing or joining a tenants' union or similar organization, or for making or expressing an intention to make, a payment of rent to an organization of unit owners pursuant to paragraph (c) of section six of chapter one hundred and eighty-three A shall be liable for damages which shall not be less than one month's rent or more than three month's rent, or the actual damages sustained by the tenant, whichever is greater, and the costs of the suit, including a reasonable attorney's fee

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent - required form and disclosures

coverage_conditions.text: residential tenant

rules.title: Maximum security deposit and upfront charges
rules.requirement: Landlords may not require more than first month's rent, last month's rent, and a security deposit equal to one month's rent at the start of a tenancy.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (security deposit); first + last + security deposit total
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span:
At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
(i) rent for the first full month of occupancy;  and,
(ii) rent for the last full month of occupancy calculated at the same rate as the first month;  and,
(iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)

rules.title: Security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at 5% per year or the lesser bank rate, paid annually for tenancies of one year or longer.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: A lessor of residential real property who holds a security deposit pursuant to this section for a period of one year or longer from the commencement of the term of the tenancy shall, beginning with the first day of the tenancy, pay interest at the rate of five per cent per year, or other such lesser amount of interest as has been received from the bank where the deposit has been held payable to the tenant at the end of each year of the tenancy

rules.title: Security deposit held in separate interest-bearing account
rules.requirement: Security deposits must be held in a separate interest-bearing bank account in Massachusetts, protected from the landlord's creditors.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: Any security deposit received by such lessor shall be held in a separate, interest-bearing account in a bank, located within the commonwealth under such terms as will place such deposit beyond the claim of creditors of the lessor, including a foreclosing mortgagee or trustee in bankruptcy, and as will provide for its transfer to a subsequent owner of said property

rules.title: Statement of condition and damage documentation required
rules.requirement: Landlords accepting security deposits must provide tenants a written statement of the premises' condition within ten days after the tenancy begins or upon receiving the deposit, whichever is later.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span: Any lessor of residential real property, or his agent, who accepts a security deposit from a tenant or prospective tenant shall, upon receipt of such security deposit, or within ten days after commencement of the tenancy, whichever is later, furnish to such tenant or prospective tenant a separate written statement of the present condition of the premises to be leased or rented

rules.title: Security deposit return and deductions
rules.requirement: Landlords must return security deposits within 30 days after the tenancy ends and may only deduct for unpaid rent, certain taxes, or actual damage excluding normal wear and tear.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to leases, rentals, occupancies or tenancies of 100 days or less in duration for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.quoted_span:
The lessor shall, within thirty days after the termination of occupancy under a tenancy-at-will or the end of the tenancy as specified in a valid written lease agreement, return to the tenant the security deposit or any balance thereof;  provided, however, that the lessor may deduct from such security deposit for the following:
(i) any unpaid rent or water charges which have not been validly withheld or deducted pursuant to any general or special law
(ii) any unpaid increase in real estate taxes which the tenant is obligated to pay pursuant to a tax escalation clause which conforms to the requirements of section fifteen C;  and
(iii) a reasonable amount necessary to repair any damage caused to the dwelling unit by the tenant or any person under the tenant's control or on the premises with the tenant's consent, reasonable wear and tear excluded
